description: An octal counter: each rising clock edge moves a single high to the next of eight outputs in turn.

inputs.text: A rising edge advances the count by one; after 7 the count returns to 0.
While this is high the count is held where it is and clock edges are ignored.
While this is high the count is held at 0 and only the first decoded output is at 10V.

outputs.text: 10V while the count is 0, 0V at every other count.
10V while the count is 1, 0V at every other count.
10V while the count is 2, 0V at every other count.
10V while the count is 3, 0V at every other count.
10V while the count is 4, 0V at every other count.
10V while the count is 5, 0V at every other count.
10V while the count is 6, 0V at every other count.
10V while the count is 7, 0V at every other count.
10V while the count is 0 to 3 and 0V while it is 4 to 7, which makes a clock at an eighth of the input rate for chaining another counter.

notes: A logic input counts as high once it rises above 2V and does not count as low again until it falls below 0.1V; a logic output is 10V for high and 0V for low.
One decoded output is always at 10V, so with nothing patched into the clock the count stays at 0 and the first output is high.
